::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Hua Hong's original Shanghai 200mm base — the three fabs the tracker missed while following the Wuxi 12-inch expansion; combined capacity ~180,000 wafers/month puts them among the largest 8-inch clusters in China. The listed A-share entity was renamed 华虹宏力 on 8 June 2026, and a formal '8-inch fab optimization & upgrade' program (2023 raise) is expanding rather than winding them down.
:::

**Chinese name:** 上海华虹宏力半导体制造有限公司 (Shànghǎi Huáhóng Hónglì Bàndǎotǐ Zhìzào Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

Mature specialty wafers — embedded non-volatile memory, power discretes, BCD analog, RF — for automotive, industrial and consumer customers.

## Why does it matter?

With TSMC and Samsung shrinking global 8-inch capacity from 2025, these fabs ran above 100% utilization through 2025 with >10% price hikes in 2026 — China's legacy-node base is now the world's marginal supplier of mature wafers, which is the strategic argument for the 2026 export-control debates over 'legacy chip' security.

## Project Timeline

- **Jun 2009** — Hua Hong merges Honghai/Hongli/Huali design+fab assets into 华虹宏力, consolidating the Zhangjiang 8-inch fabs
- **Jun 2026** — STAR-listed entity renamed 华虹宏力; 8-inch upgrade program running; utilization >100%
